newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 27.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul.
Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Nationwide strikes launched, Seoul subway unionists vow to walk out tomorrow.

- The ruling New Korea Party yesterday railroaded controversial bills on labour affair and the Agency for National Security Planning through the Assembly, bypassing opposition stonewalling by calling a blitzkrieg session at 6 a.m.
- Stocks lost ground across the board on Thursday as sentiment was badly affected by labour unrest folowing passage of a labour law.
- A nationwide strike and antigovernment protest erupted yesterday after the ruling party unilaterally railroaded a labour bill through the National Assembly
- The ruling New Korea Party railroaded two controversial bills on labour and the nation's spy agency through the National Assembly in the absence of opposition lawmakers at dawn yesterday.
